chitchat: "The body is hardware. I don't know why everyone gets so sentimental about their hardware."
"First install's always the hard one. After that you stop asking what you're losing."
description: A composed woman in a bandage-pale smock, chromed gloves that never quite come off, one magnifying ocular clipped over an eye that is already better than yours. She prices you the way a mechanic prices a trade-in — not unkindly, just accurately.

bye.text: "Come back when you're ready to upgrade." She's already prepping the chair for someone else.

how.text: "Say augment and I'll show you what your standing and your credits can carry. augment install <name> in the theatre and you'll walk out better than you came in. Fair warning: the first chrome burns out any mutation you're carrying. Chrome doesn't share a body with the old evolution — and it won't mutate again, so radiation stops being your problem."

root.text: "Sit if you like. I'm Kesh." The ocular whirs, focusing on your least-improved parts. "You've got good bones. Be a shame to die with them still original."

clothing_layers: a surgical smock the colour of a fresh bandage
chromed gloves that never quite come off
a magnifying ocular clipped over one eye

name: Dr Sable Kesh
